title: A systematic literature review of empirical research on ChatGPT in education
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the early empirical use of ChatGPT in education, focusing on how students and educators have initially incorporated the tool and what effects have been reported. The review was motivated by the rapid spread of ChatGPT and the lack of a synthesized overview of empirical studies examining its use in educational settings. The authors searched five databases and, after screening and quality appraisal, included 14 empirical studies published through April 10, 2023.

The paper does not study a single intervention but synthesizes varied uses of ChatGPT across higher education and one elementary education study. For students, ChatGPT was used as a virtual intelligent assistant, a writing and language support tool, and a resource for self-directed and personalized learning. For teachers, it was used to create lesson plans, generate quizzes, provide resources, support new activities, and improve productivity. The reviewed studies spanned multiple countries, with participants including university students, university teachers, both students and teachers, and elementary school teachers.

Overall, the review concludes that ChatGPT can support learning and teaching by providing immediate feedback, explanations, content generation, and productivity gains. At the same time, it highlights important risks, including inaccurate outputs, reduced collaborative learning, weakened creative or critical thinking when overused, and threats to academic integrity. The authors emphasize the need for structured training, clear guidelines, and further research on responsible and effective educational use.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational large language model chatbot that generates human-like text and can provide answers, explanations, feedback, and content generation support.
identified_tools.use_case: This systematic review examined empirical studies of ChatGPT in education, including how teachers used it for lesson planning, generating quizzes, providing resources, and answering student questions, as well as how students used it for feedback, writing support, and personalized learning.

findings.finding_summary: Across the 14 reviewed empirical studies, teachers used ChatGPT to create lesson plans, generate quizzes, provide additional resources, and answer student questions. The review reports that these uses helped enhance teacher productivity and efficiency and reduce workload, but it does not report quantitative effect sizes.
findings.measure: Teacher productivity, efficiency, and workload reduction as reported across included studies
findings.sample_size: 14 studies (review synthesis); primary-study sample sizes varied and were not pooled

findings.finding_summary: The review found that effective use of ChatGPT in teaching depends on structured training, support, clear rules/regulations, and ongoing discussion with policymakers and stakeholders. It also notes concerns about inaccurate information, academic integrity, and the need to redesign assessment and teaching practices.
findings.measure: Implementation conditions and broader educational implications reported across included studies
findings.sample_size: 14 studies (review synthesis); primary-study sample sizes varied and were not pooled

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review of empirical studies, so the evidence is synthesized but not a single controlled trial and does not provide pooled quantitative effects. The included studies were mainly qualitative, mixed-methods, or quasi-experimental, which supports a moderate-but-limited evidence tier.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports clear practical benefits for teacher productivity and instructional preparation, but it does not quantify effect size and also notes important implementation risks and mixed consequences. Overall impact appears promising but not clearly measurable from the review alone.
